sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Entry 170 Gyem (already held by the project from another language's check).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; entry gives location (Bauchi State, Toro LGA, Lame district), 2000 speakers (est. 2015), classification East Kainji: Northern Jos group: Lame cluster, and 'Wordlist: Blench et al (2015)' as the only source.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger, John Muniru & Luther Hon. 2015 (draft ms., January 2015; Glottolog dates 2016). Gyem: an endangered East Kainji language of Northern Nigeria. 15 pp. academia.edu item 16619179 (full document text embedded in the archived page HTML).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 3-5) = 3.1 Consonants, 3.2 Vowels, 3.3 Tones: 'Gyem has two level tones and rising and [rare] falling tones.. Almost all words begin with a low tone.' Sec. 4 adds 'tone in nouns is remarkably static. Prefixes are always low'. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the document (pp. 1-13 embedded; pp. 14-15 are wordlist datasheets).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2004. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Version submitted for the proceedings of the Hamburg meeting marking the retirement of Ludwig Gerhardt. 12 pp. (rogerblench.info, the Internet Archive 2015 capture)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the phonology/tone section describes Boze (four level tones) and tiMap; Gyem appears only in the language inventory ('Gyem (almost extinct)') and one comparative lexical table.
